review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

15:1.sourceText: Γνωρίζω δὲ ὑμῖν, ἀδελφοί, τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ὃ εὐηγγελισάμην ὑμῖν, ὃ καὶ παρελάβετε, ἐν ᾧ καὶ ἑστήκατε,
15:1.targetText: Now, brothers, I want to remind you of the gospel I preached to you, which you received, and in which you stand firm.

groups.note: Γνωρίζω ("I make known") is rendered I want to remind … of.
καί ("also") is rendered and, joining the second relative clause.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the relative ὅ ("which") unexpressed: the gospel I preached.
BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.

15:2.sourceText: δι’ οὗ καὶ σῴζεσθε, τίνι λόγῳ εὐηγγελισάμην ὑμῖν, εἰ κατέχετε, ἐκτὸς εἰ μὴ εἰκῇ ἐπιστεύσατε.
15:2.targetText: By this gospel you are saved, if you hold firmly to the word I preached to you. Otherwise, you have believed in vain.

groups.note: The relative οὗ ("which") is rendered this gospel in a new sentence.
τίνι λόγῳ ("with what word") is rendered the word.
ἐκτὸς εἰ μή ("unless") is rendered Otherwise, starting a new sentence.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.

15:3.sourceText: παρέδωκα γὰρ ὑμῖν ἐν πρώτοις, ὃ καὶ παρέλαβον, ὅτι Χριστὸς ἀπέθανεν ὑπὲρ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν κατὰ τὰς γραφάς,
15:3.targetText: For what I received I passed on to you as of first importance: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,

groups.note: ἐν πρώτοις ("among the first things") is rendered as of first importance.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:4.sourceText: καὶ ὅτι ἐτάφη, καὶ ὅτι ἐγήγερται τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ κατὰ τὰς γραφάς,
15:4.targetText: that He was buried, that He was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,

unmappedSource.reason: BSB lists the that-clauses without and; καί is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:5.sourceText: καὶ ὅτι ὤφθη Κηφᾷ, εἶτα τοῖς δώδεκα·
15:5.targetText: and that He appeared to Cephas and then to the Twelve.

groups.note: With the indeclinable δώδεκα the case word goes on the article.

15:6.sourceText: ἔπειτα ὤφθη ἐπάνω πεντακοσίοις ἀδελφοῖς ἐφάπαξ, ἐξ ὧν οἱ πλείονες μένουσιν ἕως ἄρτι, τινὲς δὲ ἐκοιμήθησαν·
15:6.targetText: After that, He appeared to more than five hundred brothers at once, most of whom are still living, though some have fallen asleep.

groups.note: οἱ πλείονες ("the greater number") is rendered most.
μένουσιν ("remain") is rendered are living.
ἕως ἄρτι ("until now") is rendered still.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:7.sourceText: ἔπειτα ὤφθη Ἰακώβῳ, εἶτα τοῖς ἀποστόλοις πᾶσιν·
15:7.targetText: Then He appeared to James, then to all the apostles.

15:8.sourceText: ἔσχατον δὲ πάντων ὡσπερεὶ τῷ ἐκτρώματι ὤφθη κἀμοί.
15:8.targetText: And last of all He appeared to me also, as to one of untimely birth.

groups.note: ἐκτρώματι ("one untimely born") is rendered one of untimely birth.
κἀμοί is καί ("also") joined to ἐμοί ("to me").

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:9.sourceText: Ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι ὁ ἐλάχιστος τῶν ἀποστόλων, ὃς οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς καλεῖσθαι ἀπόστολος, διότι ἐδίωξα τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ Θεοῦ·
15:9.targetText: For I am the least of the apostles and am unworthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.

groups.note: The relative ὅς ("who") is rendered and.
οὐκ … ἱκανός ("not fit") is rendered unworthy.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:10.sourceText: χάριτι δὲ Θεοῦ εἰμι ὅ εἰμι, καὶ ἡ χάρις αὐτοῦ ἡ εἰς ἐμὲ οὐ κενὴ ἐγενήθη, ἀλλὰ περισσότερον αὐτῶν πάντων ἐκοπίασα, οὐκ ἐγὼ δὲ ἀλλὰ ἡ χάρις τοῦ Θεοῦ σὺν ἐμοί.
15:10.targetText: But by the grace of God I am what I am, and His grace to me was not in vain. No, I worked harder than all of them—yet not I, but the grace of God that was with me.

groups.note: ἀλλά ("rather") is rendered No.
The genitive πάντων ("all") expresses the comparison, rendered than all.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a relative clause for with me; BSB's Greek text has an extra word here that N1904 lacks.

15:11.sourceText: εἴτε οὖν ἐγὼ εἴτε ἐκεῖνοι, οὕτως κηρύσσομεν καὶ οὕτως ἐπιστεύσατε.
15:11.targetText: Whether, then, it was I or they, this is what we preach, and this is what you believed.

groups.note: οὕτως ("thus") is rendered this in a cleft sentence.
οὕτως ("thus") is rendered this in a cleft sentence.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject and copula; the Greek has only ἐγώ.
English frames the clause as a cleft sentence.
English frames the clause as a cleft sentence.

15:12.sourceText: Εἰ δὲ Χριστὸς κηρύσσεται ὅτι ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγήγερται, πῶς λέγουσιν ἐν ὑμῖν τινες ὅτι ἀνάστασις νεκρῶν οὐκ ἔστιν;
15:12.targetText: But if it is preached that Christ has been raised from the dead, how can some of you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?

15:13.sourceText: εἰ δὲ ἀνάστασις νεκρῶν οὐκ ἔστιν, οὐδὲ Χριστὸς ἐγήγερται·
15:13.targetText: If there is no resurrection of the dead, then not even Christ has been raised.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ unexpressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English marks the conclusion with then.

15:14.sourceText: εἰ δὲ Χριστὸς οὐκ ἐγήγερται, κενὸν ἄρα τὸ κήρυγμα ἡμῶν, κενὴ καὶ ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν·
15:14.targetText: And if Christ has not been raised, our preaching is worthless, and so is your faith.

groups.note: κενή ("worthless") is rendered so, standing for worthless again.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves ἄρα ("then") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula.
English supplies a copula.

15:15.sourceText: εὑρισκόμεθα δὲ καὶ ψευδομάρτυρες τοῦ Θεοῦ, ὅτι ἐμαρτυρήσαμεν κατὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ ὅτι ἤγειρεν τὸν Χριστόν, ὃν οὐκ ἤγειρεν εἴπερ ἄρα νεκροὶ οὐκ ἐγείρονται.
15:15.targetText: In that case, we are also exposed as false witnesses about God. For we have testified about God that He raised Christ from the dead, but He did not raise Him if in fact the dead are not raised.

groups.note: εὑρισκόμεθα ("we are found") is rendered we are exposed as.
δέ is rendered In that case.
ἤγειρεν ("raised") is rendered raised … from the dead.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the clauses with but; the Greek continues with the relative ὅν.

15:16.sourceText: εἰ γὰρ νεκροὶ οὐκ ἐγείρονται, οὐδὲ Χριστὸς ἐγήγερται·
15:16.targetText: For if the dead are not raised, then not even Christ has been raised.

unmappedTarget.reason: English marks the conclusion with then.

15:17.sourceText: εἰ δὲ Χριστὸς οὐκ ἐγήγερται, ματαία ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν, ἔτι ἐστὲ ἐν ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις ὑμῶν.
15:17.targetText: And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile; you are still in your sins.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula; BSB's Greek text has an extra word here that N1904 lacks.

15:18.sourceText: ἄρα καὶ οἱ κοιμηθέντες ἐν Χριστῷ ἀπώλοντο.
15:18.targetText: Then those also who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished.

15:19.sourceText: εἰ ἐν τῇ ζωῇ ταύτῃ ἐν Χριστῷ ἠλπικότες ἐσμὲν μόνον, ἐλεεινότεροι πάντων ἀνθρώπων ἐσμέν.
15:19.targetText: If our hope in Christ is for this life alone, we are to be pitied more than all men.

groups.note: The actual hoped participle and we-are copula are nominalized as our hope and recast with English is. Both English pieces belong to that source predicate; the first-person subject becomes the possessive our, while the English copula states the same limitation.
The Greek comparative pitiable adjective is expressed as to be pitied more; the English passive infinitive retains the actual pity head and comparative degree.
Greek genitive all expresses the standard of comparison, rendered than all. The comparison relation belongs to that case-governed complement, not a separate Greek than word.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English word in this life.

15:20.sourceText: Νυνὶ δὲ Χριστὸς ἐγήγερται ἐκ νεκρῶν, ἀπαρχὴ τῶν κεκοιμημένων.
15:20.targetText: But Christ has indeed been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.

groups.note: Νυνί ("now", in a logical sense) is rendered indeed.

targetPhrases.text: of those who have fallen asleep

15:21.sourceText: ἐπειδὴ γὰρ δι’ ἀνθρώπου θάνατος, καὶ δι’ ἀνθρώπου ἀνάστασις νεκρῶν.
15:21.targetText: For since death came through a man, the resurrection of the dead comes also through a man.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb; the Greek clause has none.
English supplies a verb; the Greek clause has none.

15:22.sourceText: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἐν τῷ Ἀδὰμ πάντες ἀποθνήσκουσιν, οὕτως καὶ ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ πάντες ζωοποιηθήσονται.
15:22.targetText: For as in Adam all die, so in Christ all will be made alive.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.

15:23.sourceText: Ἕκαστος δὲ ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ τάγματι· ἀπαρχὴ Χριστός, ἔπειτα οἱ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ αὐτοῦ,
15:23.targetText: But each in his own turn: Christ the firstfruits; then at His coming, those who belong to Him.

groups.note: The genitive Χριστοῦ ("of Christ") is rendered who belong to Him.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:24.sourceText: εἶτα τὸ τέλος, ὅταν παραδιδοῖ τὴν βασιλείαν τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρί, ὅταν καταργήσῃ πᾶσαν ἀρχὴν καὶ πᾶσαν ἐξουσίαν καὶ δύναμιν,
15:24.targetText: Then the end will come, when He hands over the kingdom to God the Father after He has destroyed all dominion, authority, and power.

groups.note: Same verb, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
The one article τῷ governs both God and Father; BSB places the before Father.
ὅταν ("when") with the aorist is rendered after.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB renders God and Father as God the Father; καί is not rendered.
BSB joins the list with a comma; καί is not rendered here.
BSB does not repeat πᾶσαν ("all") before authority.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb; the Greek has only the end.

15:25.sourceText: δεῖ γὰρ αὐτὸν βασιλεύειν ἄχρι οὗ θῇ πάντας τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ.
15:25.targetText: For He must reign until He has put all His enemies under His feet.

groups.note: ἄχρι οὗ ("until which") is rendered until.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:26.targetText: The last enemy to be destroyed is death.

groups.note: καταργεῖται ("is being abolished") is rendered to be destroyed.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula.

15:27.sourceText: πάντα γὰρ ὑπέταξεν ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ. ὅταν δὲ εἴπῃ ὅτι πάντα ὑποτέτακται, δῆλον ὅτι ἐκτὸς τοῦ ὑποτάξαντος αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα.
15:27.targetText: For “God has put everything under His feet.” Now when it says that everything has been put under Him, this clearly does not include the One who put everything under Him.

groups.note: δῆλον ὅτι ("it is evident that") is rendered clearly.
ἐκτός ("outside, except") is rendered does not include.
The article with the participle ὑποτάξαντος ("the one who subjected") is rendered the One who put … under.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek has only the verb.
English supplies the one to whom everything is subjected.
English supplies a subject.

15:28.sourceText: ὅταν δὲ ὑποταγῇ αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα, τότε καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ Υἱὸς ὑποταγήσεται τῷ ὑποτάξαντι αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα, ἵνα ᾖ ὁ Θεὸς πάντα ἐν πᾶσιν.

15:29.sourceText: Ἐπεὶ τί ποιήσουσιν οἱ βαπτιζόμενοι ὑπὲρ τῶν νεκρῶν; εἰ ὅλως νεκροὶ οὐκ ἐγείρονται, τί καὶ βαπτίζονται ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν;
15:29.targetText: If these things are not so, what will those do who are baptized for the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why are people baptized for them?

targetPhrases.text: If these things are not so

15:30.sourceText: τί καὶ ἡμεῖς κινδυνεύομεν πᾶσαν ὥραν;
15:30.targetText: And why do we endanger ourselves every hour?

15:31.sourceText: καθ’ ἡμέραν ἀποθνῄσκω, νὴ τὴν ὑμετέραν καύχησιν, ἀδελφοί, ἣν ἔχω ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ Κυρίῳ ἡμῶν.
15:31.targetText: I face death every day, brothers, as surely as I boast about you in Christ Jesus our Lord.

groups.note: ἀποθνῄσκω ("I die") is rendered I face death.
The oath particle νή ("by") is rendered as surely as.
ὑμετέραν ("your") is rendered about you: boasting about you.
ἣν ἔχω ("which I have") is folded into I boast.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:32.sourceText: εἰ κατὰ ἄνθρωπον ἐθηριομάχησα ἐν Ἐφέσῳ, τί μοι τὸ ὄφελος; εἰ νεκροὶ οὐκ ἐγείρονται, φάγωμεν καὶ πίωμεν, αὔριον γὰρ ἀποθνήσκομεν.
15:32.targetText: If I fought wild beasts in Ephesus for human motives, what did I gain? If the dead are not raised,  “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.”

groups.note: κατὰ ἄνθρωπον ("according to man") is rendered for human motives.
τί μοι τὸ ὄφελος ("what is the profit to me") is rendered what did I gain.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:33.sourceText: μὴ πλανᾶσθε· φθείρουσιν ἤθη χρηστὰ ὁμιλίαι κακαί.
15:33.targetText: Do not be deceived: “Bad company corrupts good character.”

15:34.sourceText: ἐκνήψατε δικαίως καὶ μὴ ἁμαρτάνετε· ἀγνωσίαν γὰρ Θεοῦ τινες ἔχουσιν· πρὸς ἐντροπὴν ὑμῖν λαλῶ.
15:34.targetText: Sober up as you ought, and stop sinning; for some of you are ignorant of God. I say this to your shame.

groups.note: δικαίως ("rightly") is rendered as you ought.
μή with the present imperative is rendered stop.
ἀγνωσίαν … ἔχουσιν ("have ignorance") is rendered are ignorant.
ὑμῖν ("to you") is rendered your.

unmappedTarget.reason: English specifies some of you; the Greek has only τινες ("some").
English supplies an object.

15:35.sourceText: Ἀλλὰ ἐρεῖ τις Πῶς ἐγείρονται οἱ νεκροί; ποίῳ δὲ σώματι ἔρχονται;

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ unexpressed.

15:36.sourceText: ἄφρων, σὺ ὃ σπείρεις, οὐ ζωοποιεῖται ἐὰν μὴ ἀποθάνῃ·
15:36.targetText: You fool! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies.

15:37.sourceText: καὶ ὃ σπείρεις, οὐ τὸ σῶμα τὸ γενησόμενον σπείρεις, ἀλλὰ γυμνὸν κόκκον εἰ τύχοι σίτου ἤ τινος τῶν λοιπῶν·
15:37.targetText: And what you sow is not the body that will be, but just a seed, perhaps of wheat or something else.

groups.note: The article with the participle γενησόμενον ("the one that will be") is rendered that will be.
γυμνόν ("bare") is rendered just.
εἰ τύχοι ("if it should happen") is rendered perhaps.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not repeat σπείρεις ("you sow"); English uses is.

15:38.targetText: But God gives it a body as He has designed, and to each kind of seed He gives its own body.

groups.note: BSB repeats He gives in the second clause.

The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:49.sourceText: καὶ καθὼς ἐφορέσαμεν τὴν εἰκόνα τοῦ χοϊκοῦ, φορέσωμεν καὶ τὴν εἰκόνα τοῦ ἐπουρανίου.
15:49.targetText: And just as we have borne the likeness of the earthly man, so also shall we bear the likeness of the heavenly man.

groups.note: Same verb; BSB's Greek has another form of it here, rendered shall we bear (N1904's subjunctive means "let us bear").

15:50.sourceText: Τοῦτο δέ φημι, ἀδελφοί, ὅτι σὰρξ καὶ αἷμα βασιλείαν Θεοῦ κληρονομῆσαι οὐ δύναται, οὐδὲ ἡ φθορὰ τὴν ἀφθαρσίαν κληρονομεῖ.
15:50.targetText: Now I declare to you, brothers, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, nor does the perishable inherit the imperishable.

groups.note: οὐ δύναται ("is not able") is rendered cannot.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves τοῦτο ("this") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the hearers; the Greek has no ὑμῖν here.

15:51.sourceText: ἰδοὺ μυστήριον ὑμῖν λέγω· πάντες οὐ κοιμηθησόμεθα, πάντες δὲ ἀλλαγησόμεθα,
15:51.targetText: Listen, I tell you a mystery: We will not all sleep, but we will all be changed—

15:52.sourceText: ἐν ἀτόμῳ, ἐν ῥιπῇ ὀφθαλμοῦ, ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ σάλπιγγι· σαλπίσει γάρ, καὶ οἱ νεκροὶ ἐγερθήσονται ἄφθαρτοι, καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀλλαγησόμεθα.
15:52.targetText: in an instant, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.

groups.note: σαλπίσει ("it will trumpet") is rendered the trumpet will sound.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB joins the clauses with a comma; καί is not rendered here.

15:53.sourceText: δεῖ γὰρ τὸ φθαρτὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσασθαι ἀφθαρσίαν καὶ τὸ θνητὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσασθαι ἀθανασίαν.
15:53.targetText: For the perishable must be clothed with the imperishable, and the mortal with immortality.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the demonstrative τοῦτο ("this") untranslated.
BSB does not repeat be clothed in the second clause.

15:54.sourceText: ὅταν δὲ τὸ φθαρτὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσηται ἀφθαρσίαν καὶ τὸ θνητὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσηται ἀθανασίαν, τότε γενήσεται ὁ λόγος ὁ γεγραμμένος Κατεπόθη ὁ θάνατος εἰς νῖκος.
15:54.targetText: When the perishable has been clothed with the imperishable and the mortal with immortality, then the saying that is written will come to pass: “Death has been swallowed up in victory.”

groups.note: The article with the participle γεγραμμένος ("the one written") is rendered that is written.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ unexpressed.
BSB leaves the demonstrative τοῦτο ("this") untranslated.
BSB does not repeat has been clothed in the second clause.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

15:55.sourceText: ποῦ σου, θάνατε, τὸ νῖκος; ποῦ σου, θάνατε, τὸ κέντρον;
15:55.targetText: “Where, O Death, is your victory? Where, O Death, is your sting?”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula.
English supplies a copula.

15:56.sourceText: τὸ δὲ κέντρον τοῦ θανάτου ἡ ἁμαρτία, ἡ δὲ δύναμις τῆς ἁμαρτίας ὁ νόμος·
15:56.targetText: The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula.
English supplies a copula.

15:57.sourceText: τῷ δὲ Θεῷ χάρις τῷ διδόντι ἡμῖν τὸ νῖκος διὰ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
15:57.targetText: But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ!

groups.note: The article with the participle διδόντι ("the one giving") is rendered who gives.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb; the Greek has none.

15:58.sourceText: Ὥστε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί, ἑδραῖοι γίνεσθε, ἀμετακίνητοι, περισσεύοντες ἐν τῷ ἔργῳ τοῦ Κυρίου πάντοτε, εἰδότες ὅτι ὁ κόπος ὑμῶν οὐκ ἔστιν κενὸς ἐν Κυρίῳ.
15:58.targetText: Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast and immovable. Always excel in the work of the Lord, because you know that your labor in the Lord is not in vain.

groups.note: The participle περισσεύοντες ("abounding") is rendered as the command excel.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the two adjectives with and; the Greek has no καί here.
English supplies a subject for the participle εἰδότες ("knowing").
